rv.q: Fleetwood-Jourdain’s work here should not be missed.
Orlandersmith’s exploration of the tragedy from a variety of perspectives offers no false hope for racial harmony.
This performance is one of those productions that could go right for your gut and keep you enthralled, but it might leave you wishing it had been delivered in a more conventional dramatic style.
“Until the Flood” is the pinnacle of perfection!
It is just all laid out there on the stage for us to think about for ourselves in this not-to-be-missed Fleetwood-Jourdain production.

cn.t: Orlandersmith's powerful monologue play about Ferguson's Michael Brown shooting earns praise for its raw, heartfelt portrayals of racial tensions, with critics calling it moving and provocative despite its heavy subject matter.
